result.markdown: # R processing layer {.unnumbered} This document translates the contents of lab 2 in R. The source Quarto document can be found in [`_labs/lab02/R/model-vetiver-r.qmd`](https://github.com/mjfrigaard/do4ds-labs/blob/main/_labs/lab02/R/model-vetiver-r.qmd). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fs::dir_tree("_labs/lab02/R/") ## _labs/lab02/R/ ## └── model-vetiver-r.qmd ``` ::: ## Load packages ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(palmerpenguins) library(plumber) library(dplyr) library(duckdb) library(fastDummies) library(vetiver) library(pins) ``` ::: ## Get Data Load the `palmerpenguins` data, create a connection with `dbConnect()`, register the R data frame with `duckdb`, create the `penguins` table: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins_data <- palmerpenguins::penguins con <- dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), "my-db.duckdb") duckdb_register(con, "penguins_data", penguins_data) dbExecute(con, "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE penguins AS SELECT * FROM penguins_data") ``` ::: Omit missing, disconnect from DB: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM penguins") |> na.omit() dbDisconnect(con) ``` ::: View top rows of `df`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} head(df, 3) ``` ::: ## Define Model and Fit Create dummy variables (one-hot encoding) and fit linear regression model. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} X <- df |> select(bill_length_mm, species, sex) |> dummy_cols( select_columns = c("species", "sex"), remove_first_dummy = TRUE) |> select(-species, -sex) y <- df$body_mass_g model <- lm(y ~ ., data = X) ``` ::: ## Get some information ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} r_squared <- summary(model)$r.squared intercept <- coef(model)[1] coefficients <- coef(model)[-1] column_names <- names(X) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cat("R^2:", r_squared, "\n") cat("Intercept:", intercept, "\n") cat("Columns:", paste(column_names, collapse = ", "), "\n") cat("Coefficients:", paste(coefficients, collapse = ", "), "\n") ``` ::: ## Turn into Vetiver Model ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} v <- vetiver_model(model, model_name = "penguin_model") ``` ::: Below we can see the model information stored in the `models/` folder: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} fs::dir_tree("_labs/lab02/R/models/") ## _labs/lab02/R/models/ ## └── penguin_model ## └── 20250923T141916Z-cca3d ## ├── data.txt ## └── penguin_model.rds ``` ::: ## Save to Board ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} model_board <- board_folder("./models") vetiver_pin_write(model_board, v) ``` ::: ## Turn model into API Unlike Python, we'll need to create a plumber router from `plumber::pr()` to pass to the `vetiver_api()` (along with the deployable `vetiver_model()` object). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} app <- pr() |> vetiver_api(v) ``` :::
